name: Authorization checks must not be removed from record accessors
content: Any function that retrieves a user-owned record MUST verify the caller owns that record before returning it. If a function accepts both a caller identity and a record identifier, it must compare the record owner against the caller and raise an authorization error on mismatch. Removing, weakening, or short-circuiting that ownership comparison is an insecure direct object reference (CWE-639): any authenticated caller can then read or mutate another account's data by supplying its id. A caller-identity parameter that becomes unused after a change is direct evidence the check was dropped. This applies transitively: if a mutating operation relies on such an accessor for its authorization, weakening the accessor escalates to an unauthorized write.
good_examples: The accessor compares the record owner against the caller identity and raises an authorization error when they differ, before returning the record.
bad_examples: The accessor returns the record without comparing its owner to the caller identity, leaving the caller-identity parameter unused.
